input.title: fix: preserve independent mounted shield artwork and callbacks
input.body:
## Summary

```text
each shield mount
  → owns its cached size, retained hit clip and current film
  → queues its own cleanup callback
all mounts
  → share the tank's immunity flag and latest first-use hit pointer
```

Continues the recreation backlog with source-backed mounted-shield ownership. Native painting, mock rings and geometric contact retain the same child identities and stage clocks.

## Evidence

- **Before:** the staggered-mount regression finds one shared `shield-hit`/`shield-film` pair.
  **After:** both mounts retain separate hit/film pairs; one mount's callback removes its own current film and clears shared immunity.
- Covers staggered sizes, independent callbacks, older hit instances, same-mount retrigger ownership, arrival and paused clocks. Artwork/contact fixtures inspect instance retention and real damage after immunity clears.
- Formatting, TypeScript, 421 tests / 5570 assertions and production build pass. All 54 selected mock/synthetic and affected native browser cases pass; both shield galleries inspected. Full scope is recorded in the fidelity ledger.
- Recovered `AGunShield` and `_-Zx` supply the contract. Cleanup tolerates already absent films; original-runtime event interleaving, full live-child sizing and broader parity remain explicit limits.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

**Blast Radius:** protection

Multiple shield mounts now have independent artwork and cleanup; immunity remains shared. No proprietary media or extracted vectors are committed.

## Summary

```text
Stage → tank/projectile → part/attachment → nested leaf
  carry the full inverse linear matrix
  local stroke width = max(authored width, inverse column lengths)
  keep declared bounds rejection and round geometric caps/joins
```

Corrects positive thin strokes at reduced scales, including game zoom. Creator selection and retained/stateless projectile contact use the same transform calculation. CSS/DPR scaling stays outside this geometry contract.

## Evidence

- **Before:** the new browser regression misses four expected thin-stroke hits at full scale, half scale, nested unequal scaling and reflection.
  **After:** those hits pass alongside misses/bounds, enlarged widths, singular transforms, endpoint distance, rotated/scaled tank parts, game zoom and retained/stateless projectile checks.
- Pinned Ruffle source and controlled replay corroborate the width calculation. `hit-test-probe.py --thin-strokes` reproduces the recorded 1220-byte SHA256; the default 970-byte payload is unchanged. No SWFs or artwork committed. Adobe behavior and exact twip/boundary semantics remain explicit limits.
- `bun run format`, `bun run check`: 417 tests, 5543 assertions. Production build passes. 54 broad browser cases pass; after isolating cached synthetic fixture data, a fresh build and all six contact/native creator cases pass. Full validation scope and remaining limits are recorded in the fidelity ledger.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

**Blast Radius:** collision

May change projectile interception near thin contours. Painted artwork is unchanged; geometry stays within declared leaf bounds.

# Goal: faithfully recreate Bubble Tanks 3

Continue building a faithful, one-to-one recreation of the original Bubble Tanks 3 Flash game in `/home/ian/Projects/ianwijma/open-bubble-tank`. The intended result is an offline game whose appearance, animation, controls, sound and gameplay are indistinguishable from the original, except for explicitly documented removals and usability additions.

The reverse-engineering documentation and original implementation evidence are in `/home/ian/Projects/ianwijma/documented-bubble-tank-3`. # Skill Library

Skills are NOT loaded into context automatically. They live in a managed library
and must be loaded on demand, per task.

## Workflow — query whenever a skill might help

1. Whenever you think a skill might be needed — before starting a task, when the
   work shifts into new territory, or when unsure — summarize the task into a
   1–3 sentence description (include key technologies, file types, and the goal),
   then run:

   ```sh
   skill-library query "<task description>"
   ```

   This fires very often, and that is fine: a query is cheap; a missed skill is
   not.

2. If matches are returned: Read each returned `path` (absolute paths to skill
   markdown files) and absorb the instructions **before** working on the task.
3. If `matches` is empty, proceed on your own judgment.
4. For a rapid follow-up that trivially continues the same task with the same
   context, reusing the skills already read is acceptable; when in doubt,
   re-query.

title: use client
description: Learn how to use the use client directive to render a component on the client.
---

The `'use client'` directive declares an entry point for the components to be rendered on the **client side** and should be used when creating interactive user interfaces (UI) that require client-side JavaScript capabilities, such as state management, event handling, and access to browser APIs. This is a React feature.

> **Good to know:**
>
> You do not need to add the `'use client'` directive to every file that contains Client Components. You only need to add it to the files whose components you want to render directly within Server Components. The `'use client'` directive defines the [server and client boundary](/docs/app/guides/server-and-client-boundary), and the components exported from such a file serve as entry points to the client.

## Usage

To declare an entry point for the Client Components, add the `'use client'` directive **at the top of the file**, before any imports. The directive applies to the entire module and cannot be placed inside a component or function:
